note: The three banks are BBVA México, Banamex and HSBC México, chosen as the largest card issuers whose terms could be read: Santander México's site refused the request (403, Akamai) and Banorte's didn't answer, so HSBC, the next large issuer, stands in. BBVA México's summaries for each of its eleven personal credit cards (each issued 4 August 2026), read in full: the rate written is the balance-weighted average annual rate the bank states for the card (the rate itself is variable, the TIIE de fondeo plus a margin); the card administration fee for the holder is charged on taking the card and at each yearly renewal (Start and Mi Primera Tarjeta charge none); cash withdrawals cost a share of the sum (7%, the Platinum's 4.50%; Crea, Start and Mi Primera list none); the late payment penalty is a fixed sum each time the minimum isn't paid by its due date (Mi Primera's is nothing). The Platinum's fee is waived from its second anniversary on 750,000 pesos of purchases a year, a condition tied to the card's age that isn't written, so the fee is charged in full. The summaries say the payment is due 20 days after the statement date, which is not the longest a purchase goes without interest, so no grace is written; they state no minimum payment formula, foreign transaction fee or penalty rate. Banamex's costs and charges page for each of its fifteen personal credit cards (CAT calculated 27 July 2026, valid to 27 January 2027; LineUp's calculated 27 May 2026): the weighted average annual rate, the holder's administration fee (charged monthly on most cards, yearly on Beyond and The Home Depot; Joy charges none, its 149-peso monthly inactivity penalty, a condition the game doesn't check, isn't written), the cash withdrawal fee as a share of the sum (a promotional figure valid to 27 January 2027, the only one stated), and the late payment penalty. La Comer Card's table gives a monthly fee of 102.50 pesos while its CAT footnote says the administration costs nothing; the table's fee is written. B-smart's page states only its rate and monthly fee. The penalty rate (the ordinary rate times a factor of up to 1.5) isn't a stated figure and isn't written. HSBC México's digital brochures for seven of its cards (CAT valid to 7 December 2026; One Plus to 15 December 2027) and its Travel One Gold and Platinum pages (CAT from 28 October 2026): the weighted average rate, the holder's administration fee (monthly on 2Now, Zero and VIVA, waived in a month with 3,500 pesos (2Now) or 300 pesos (Zero, VIVA) of card use, written as spending), the cash withdrawal fee as a share and the late payment penalty. The Travel One pages state only the rate and the yearly fee. All three banks state their fees before VAT, which is added at a rate none of the documents states, so no tax is written; no document states a minimum payment, a grace period, an over-limit fee or a foreign transaction fee.
